latest_census.notes: The 2024 census is the latest. DoP publishes a '2024 Provisional Result' (https://dop.gov.mm/sites/dop.gov.mm/files/publication_docs/2024_provisional_result_eng.pdf) and a '2024 Main Report' category (https://www.dop.gov.mm/en/publication-category/2024-main-report). Provisional-result snippet: 51,316,756 residents as of 30 Sep 2024, of whom only 32,191,407 were enumerated and 19,125,349 were 'estimated' for unenumerated areas -- so it is a partial count. A Wikipedia snippet ('Hinduism in Myanmar') attributes a national 2024 figure (0.6%, about 189,718 Hindus) to it, which suggests religion was asked, but no search result showed a 2024 religion or ethnicity table by state/region; the search intended to check this ('Myanmar 2024 census main report religion by state and region') did not run because the session's search budget was exhausted. The well-documented census is 2014 -- see earlier_census.

earlier_census.notes: Religion: asked of everyone and published in Census Report Volume 2-C 'The Union Report: Religion' (launched July 2016), 'at the Union level and by State/Region' (ReliefWeb snippet). Ethnicity: asked, but the tables were withheld -- 'while the religion section was released in June 2016, the ethnic population figures continued to be withheld' (Irrawaddy / Myanmar Times / TNI results); no search result shows them ever being released. Language: no search result mentioned a language question either way; the check ('Myanmar 2014 census questionnaire language question') did not run (budget exhausted), so this is unestablished. The map's national record already marks language pct as not_available.

already_in_map: Per docs/SOURCES.md (USCB subnational series table and the Myanmar bullets), admin1 (14/14) and admin2 (70/74) religion and ethnicity are already filled from the US Census Bureau workbook: religion from the 2014 census (15 states/regions, 80 districts) and 'ethnicity' from the DoP 2018 Township Profiles Table 14 (reference April 2017, Ethnic Nationalities Living, 40 named groups, not a census). Kenya/Uganda are not in that series; Myanmar is. The 4 unfilled admin2 shapes are most plausibly districts created after the workbook's district list -- the Loilen District snippet says 'in 2022, most of its townships were split off to form new districts', and Mongmit District 'was created by decree in 2015'.

tier_reason: The A-grade route (USCB XLSX of 2014 census religion by state/district plus the 2017 Township Profiles ethnicity) is already built per SOURCES.md. Everything not yet in the map is B-grade: the official Vol 2-C is a PDF at the level already filled; township-level religion exists only as MIMU Excel that must be aggregated to districts through a crosswalk; census ethnicity has never been published from any Myanmar census; the 2024 census's religion tables are unverified and it enumerated only 32.2M of 51.3M people; language is unestablished.
recommended_action: Nothing found here improves on the workbook already joined. Two follow-ups when search budget allows: (1) open the DoP '2024 Main Report' category page to see whether a religion-by-state/region table exists -- if so it would supersede 2014 at admin1 and needs the 32.2M-enumerated caveat recorded; (2) open MIMU baseline-datasets to check for a religion-by-township sheet, then map the 4 unfilled admin2 districts (likely 2015/2022 splits such as Mongmit and the Loilen offshoots) to their townships. Language should stay declared unknown until the 2014 questionnaire is checked.

summary: Myanmar's admin1 and 70 of 74 admin2 already carry 2014-census religion and 2017 Township-Profile ethnicity from the US Census Bureau workbook, and nothing surfaced that beats it. The 2014 census asked ethnicity but the tables were withheld and never released, so no census ethnicity exists at any level; religion was published in Volume 2-C (PDF, by state/region) and is digitised to township level by MIMU in Excel, which could fill the last four districts only via a township-to-district crosswalk. The 2024 census has provisional and main-report pages on dop.gov.mm but enumerated only 32.2M of 51.3M people; whether it publishes religion subnationally could not be checked before the search budget ran out. Language was not established either way. Tier B: what remains is costly, and the one potential upgrade (2024 religion by state/region) is unverified.
